# Work Lifecycle Roadmap

<!-- Generated by repo-harness-builder; source: core/docs:3.0 -->

<!-- doc-role:lifecycle-owner -->

This roadmap is the canonical lifecycle owner. Track only non-trivial work with immutable `RH-W-####` IDs. Each record keeps origin, justified `P0` to `P3` priority, dependencies, status, completed and remaining work, additions, exclusions, deferrals, rejections, evidence, decision history, and an observable next advancement condition.

## Lifecycle Rules
<!-- doc-role:lifecycle-rules -->

- Status is one of `proposed`, `ready`, `active`, `blocked`, `deferred`, `completed`, `excluded`, or `rejected`.
- `blocked` names its blocker, `deferred` names its advancement condition, and terminal records use remaining work `none`.
- `excluded` is reconsiderable outside current scope. `rejected` is intentionally declined until an explicit later decision supersedes it.
- Update this owner, current-state projection, localized peers, and Engram topic `work/RH-W-####` in the same work unit when reality changes.

## Active Records
<!-- doc-role:active-records -->

- Per-pixel / sector control: not found (APK notes, wall-led and LED_UNION READMEs show whole-strip frames only; `odd/tasks/led-lab.md` L28). The 50 green / 50 yellow / 50 red test stays preview-only. Optional: capture the vendor DIY/graffiti screen if available.
- Firmware: the unpopulated header hole B is the Bluetrum one-wire download port; the ROM bootloader answers with chip ID `BLUEMATE` (L44-L46). Flash read is blocked: the public bluetrum-tools blob does not run on MATE (L45). ROM `MEM_READ` works (L49-L51): the 3 KB plaintext boot code was read and CRC-verified. Open (L51): a full flash read needs a custom RAM blob and code analysis with no guarantee; continue or pause is the user's choice. Use the gold or blue adapter; red is dead (L50). Every risky step needs user approval (`odd/tasks/led-lab.md` S4); never run write/erase.
- Windows BLE: UB500 Plus test done (lab L48); Windows cannot discover the controller's characteristics through its Bluetooth stack. Open option (untested, needs user decision): bypass the Windows stack with a dedicated USB dongle (for example Bumble over WinUSB).
- Bench tests that need the user at the strip (Android Chrome lab): range, preset modes, native effect catalog (210 IDs).
- Capture remaining vendor frames: music/mic (`0B`, `0C`), timer (`10`), 10 m strip.
- Phone design: v3 skins in `design/deleluz-mobile-v3/` and Stitch project "DeleLuz v3"; resume after device knowledge.
- First commit and private GitHub repository, when the user asks.
